title: fix(cli): os migrate plan and apply name each drop gate's command, never --allow-destructive, for the drops apply refuses
body:
Fixes #24958
Clause-②: no

`os migrate plan` and `os migrate apply` no longer offer `--allow-destructive` as the way on for a drop that `os migrate apply` refuses whatever flag is passed. Three of `apply`'s drop gates refuse the whole `--allow-destructive` run while such a drop is in it: `sys_account.issuer` while its retirement pre-flight does not pass, `sys_comment.reactions` while no verified run of `os migrate comment-reactions --apply` is recorded, and an `organization_id` drop while the organization-ownership ceremony has not verified (ADR-0131 D10 item 5). Each such drop is still listed and counted as drift in both commands. Its line names what it waits for, the footer names that gate's commands, and no line offers a re-run with `--allow-destructive` while one is held. A database with no held drop prints what it printed before, byte for byte, in both commands. The `--json` documents, the exit codes and every refusal (rule and text) are unchanged.

## What changed

- `packages/cli/src/utils/apply-drop-gates.ts` (new): `apply`'s drop gates as the doors read them.
  - The two predicates that were inline in `apply.ts` move here unchanged: `isAccountIssuerDrop` and `isCommentReactionsDrop`. `isCeremonyOrganizationDrop` asks the drop gate's own `ceremonyOrganizationColumnDrops`. `apply` asks the first two from here.
  - `DropGateReads` makes each gate's read at most once per run: `probeAccountIdentityCollisions` (plugin-auth), `readCommentReactionsConversion` and `readOrganizationOwnershipMarker`, the same functions `apply`'s gates call. The listing and the gate share that read, so they cannot answer differently, and a held run reads each gate once, as before. A read that throws is remembered as thrown, so the issuer gate's "could not read" refusal is unchanged.
  - `APPLY_DROP_GATES`: one row per gate, in `apply`'s order, with its predicate, how it judges its read, the listing line and the footer line. There is no second inventory, dialect or table list.
  - `readHeldDrops`, `describeDriftEntries` and `describeHeldDrops` generalise PR #24954's `ceremonyHeldDrops`, `describeWithCeremonyHolds` and `describeCeremonyHold`. A gate that judges no listed entry is never read. The `organization_id` lines keep PR #24954's text byte for byte.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts`: the plan asks the module instead of its three local helpers (removed), so the issuer and reactions gates join the ceremony's.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts`:
  - The human face reads the held drops before the listing, like the driver's apply limits, and never under `--json`.
  - The listing names each held drop's gate. While a drop is held, the pre-prompt line is `N destructive change(s) will be SKIPPED, and a re-run with --allow-destructive cannot include them yet:` followed by one line per gate, and the post-apply line is `Skipped N destructive change(s); a re-run with --allow-destructive cannot include them yet (see above).`
  - The gates ask the moved predicates and the shared reads. Their refusal rule, refusal text, `--json` documents and exit codes are untouched.
- `packages/cli/test/migrate-drop-gate-remedies.pin.test.ts` (new, unit tier): the enumeration pin, described below.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.organization-ownership-refusal.test.ts`, `apply.account-issuer-json-refusal.test.ts`: fixture triage. Each fixture spelled the drift entry's finding as `description`, a key `ManagedDriftEntry` does not declare, and carried no `message`, which it requires. The listing now reads `message` for a held drop, and on these fixtures it threw before the gate. Both org human-face cases went red (the refusal never printed). The issuer human-face control stayed green, exiting 1 from that throw rather than from its refusal. Both fixtures now carry the differ's `message`, and the issuer control also asserts that its refusal printed.
- `.changeset/24958-migrate-drop-gate-remedies.md`: `@objectstack/cli` patch.

## Measured at the public door

Setup:
- **Databases.** Copies of a SQLite database that a `create-objectstack@17.7.0` app had booted once (43 tables carrying `organization_id`, `sys_comment.reactions` present, no ceremony marker, no reactions conversion recorded, no `sys_account.issuer`). Variants were shaped by hand:
  - `held`: one comment carrying a stored reaction.
  - `reactions`: as `held`, plus a verified ceremony marker row.
  - `orgonly`: a verified reactions-conversion row.
  - `issuer`: both rows verified, plus the legacy `issuer` column, the `(provider_id, account_id)` unique index dropped, and a second account row sharing the first one's key.
  - `issuerclean`: as `issuer` with no second row.
  - `verified`: both rows verified.
  - `fresh18`: a fresh 18 database plus one orphan column.
- **How it was run.** This repository's CLI, built at `62bc12930` (main) and then at this branch, from a minimal project directory with `OS_AUTH_SECRET` set so the auth family composes, stdin from `/dev/null`. Every run used its own fresh copy.

The card's three mechanism assumptions, on main:

1. **Confirmed.** On `held`, `os migrate apply --yes` exits 0 and lists each `organization_id` drop as `sys_job.organization_id: column exists in the database but not in metadata (orphaned) — "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it.`, then prints `⚠ 22 destructive change(s) will be SKIPPED (re-run with --allow-destructive to include them).` and, after applying, `⚠ Skipped 22 destructive change(s) (re-run with --allow-destructive to include them).` That re-run is refused, exit 1. On `held` the reactions gate refuses it first. On `orgonly` the drop gate refuses it: `✗ Refusing this --allow-destructive run: it would drop organization_id from sys_job, sys_job_queue, … Nothing in this run was applied.`
2. **Confirmed.** On `reactions`, `os migrate plan` lists `sys_comment.reactions: column exists in the database but not in metadata (orphaned) — "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it.` and closes with `Apply with: os migrate apply (add --allow-destructive for drops / tightenings)`. `os migrate apply --allow-destructive --yes` exits 1: `✗ Refusing to drop sys_comment.reactions: … Run "os migrate comment-reactions" to preview, then "os migrate comment-reactions --apply"; once it reports the run verified, re-run this command.` The gate's predicate moved out of `apply.ts` unchanged: the same reads, the same answer, the same refusal text (the refusal lines and exit codes below are identical).
3. **It does, so it is in scope.** On `issuer`, the plan lists `sys_account.issuer: column exists in the database but not in metadata (orphaned) — "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it.` with the same footer, and `apply --allow-destructive --yes` exits 1: `✗ Refusing to drop sys_account.issuer: … Resolve them, then re-run "os migrate account-issuer" as the post-check before applying.` The control `issuerclean` passes the pre-flight (`✓ sys_account.issuer retirement pre-flight: clean over 1 row(s).`) and applies, exit 0, so there the plan's `--allow-destructive` is right and is kept.

After, on this branch. The `held` plan's footer:

```text
  ℹ 28 change(s): 6 safe, 0 needs-confirm, 22 destructive
  Apply with: os migrate apply
  ⚠ sys_comment.reactions above is where reactions were stored before they became sys_comment_reaction records, and no verified run of "os migrate comment-reactions --apply" is recorded on this database, so "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" refuses every run until one is (the other 21 destructive change(s) above wait for it too). Run "os migrate comment-reactions" to preview, then "os migrate comment-reactions --apply"; it carries them into records and records the run verified.
  ⚠ 8 organization_id drop(s) above are the organization-ownership ceremony's, and it has not verified on this database, so "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" refuses every run until it has (the other 14 destructive change(s) above wait for it too). Run "os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN" to write and review its plan, take a backup, then "os migrate organization-ownership --apply --plan-file PLAN --backup-taken"; it drops these columns itself.
```

`os migrate apply --yes` on `held` prints the same two gate lines under `⚠ 22 destructive change(s) will be SKIPPED, and a re-run with --allow-destructive cannot include them yet:`, then `⚠ Skipped 22 destructive change(s); a re-run with --allow-destructive cannot include them yet (see above).` The held entries read:

```text
sys_comment.reactions: column exists in the database but not in metadata (orphaned) — a drop that waits for "os migrate comment-reactions" to carry any reactions stored in it into sys_comment_reaction records, and no verified run is recorded on this database (see below).
sys_account.issuer: column exists in the database but not in metadata (orphaned) — a drop that waits for its retirement pre-flight, "os migrate account-issuer", which does not pass on this database (see below).
```

and the `issuer` footer: `⚠ sys_account.issuer above is the retired account issuer, and its retirement pre-flight finds 1 (provider_id, account_id) key(s) held by more than one row on this database, so "os migrate apply --allow-destructive" refuses every run until it passes (the other 23 destructive change(s) above wait for it too). Run "os migrate account-issuer" for its report, resolve what it lists, then re-run it as the post-check.`

**Byte for byte, main against this branch, 24 runs.** Log timestamps, the duration line and the per-run copy's directory were normalised before comparing. "Refusals and exit" compares every `Refusing` line plus the exit code.

| database | command | diff lines | refusals and exit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `held` | `plan` · `apply --yes` · `apply --allow-destructive --yes` | 3 · 24 · 20 | identical |
| `reactions` | the same three | 5 · 7 · 3 | identical |
| `issuer` | the same three | 5 · 7 · 3 | identical |
| `orgonly` | the same three | 0 · 21 · 17 | identical |
| `verified` | the same three | 0 · 0 · 0 | identical |
| `issuerclean` | the same three | 0 · 0 · 0 | identical |
| `fresh18` | `plan` · `apply --yes` | 0 · 0 | identical |
| `held` · `verified` | `plan --json` · `apply --yes --json` | 0 · 0 · 0 · 0 | identical |

Every differing line is a held entry's line, a gate's footer line, or a skip line. `orgonly`'s plan is identical because PR #24954 already handled it, and the generalised code reproduces that text.

## The enumeration pin: red on main, then green; one ablation

`packages/cli/test/migrate-drop-gate-remedies.pin.test.ts`, 33 cases.
- **Discovery.** It reads every `message: 'refused_…'` from `apply.ts` and requires each to be claimed by a roster row (or by `refused_unloadable_host_config`, which is not a drop gate). The rows must equal `APPLY_DROP_GATES`, in order, and each row's entry must be judged by its own gate and no other. A new gate's refusal fails the first case, by name, until it has a row, and its row's cases fail until the module reads it.
- **Per gate, per held state** (issuer: colliding keys, and `sys_account` unreadable; reactions and the ceremony: no row, and an unverified row):
  - `plan` lists and counts the entry, its line carries no `--allow-destructive`, and the footer names every command of the gate's remedy and offers `--allow-destructive` for nothing.
  - `apply --yes`: the same listing line and footer; no line offers a re-run with `--allow-destructive`; the safe work still applies.
  - `apply --allow-destructive --yes`: the same listing line, then the gate's own refusal, exit 1, nothing written, naming the same commands. The gate's read was made once.
- **Controls.** A released gate (clean pre-flight, verified row) prints what it always printed in both commands, and its read WAS made. No gated drop: neither command reads anything.
- **`--json`.** The plan document carries the differ's messages and reads no gate.
- The reads are the gates' real ones over a fake `objectql` service holding the rows. The boot, the occupancy probe and the one-shot exit are replaced. The subjects resolve through relative `src/` imports, not a package's `exports`, so no `dist/` preflight applies.

| leg | result |
| :--- | :--- |
| `apply.ts` and `plan.ts` at `62bc12930` (main), tree only, the new module and pin kept | 18 failed, 15 passed. The 16 held cases fail on the listing line (`not to contain '--allow-destructive'`). The ceremony's two plan cases pass: PR #24954 already handled them. The issuer and reactions plan controls fail only at their final read-count assertion, because main never reads those gates. Restored: blobs `2d4a0663659a` and `5d66675a3243` equal HEAD's, `git diff HEAD` is empty and `git status` is clean. |
| branch | 33 passed |
| ablation, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the reactions gate's judgement `.verified ? null` changed to `.verified !== undefined /* ABLATION */ ? null` (the read made, its verdict ignored) | 6 failed (exactly the six reactions held cases), 27 passed. Anchor 1 to 0, blob `d93231fab096` to `bdb42c39683d`. Restored: blob equals HEAD's `d93231fab096`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. |

## Local verification

All at the final head `fc8973ea8d`, a clean merge of `origin/main` (`73432299c`; no incoming file under `packages/cli` or the gates' packages), unless a line says otherwise.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0, test layer included (`check:test-typecheck: OK`).
- `@objectstack/cli` unit tier (`vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`): `Test Files 317 passed (317)`, `Tests 4717 passed (4717)`, at `8bb7ff69ff`, the branch's last own commit before the merge. At `fc8973ea8d` the pin, its neighbours and the tier partition re-ran green: `plan.apply-limit`, both gate-refusal tests, `migrate-confirmation-exit.pin`, `exit-signal.pin` and `vitest-tiers-partition`, `Tests 225 passed`.
- Integration tier: this diff touches no integration file, spawn entry or boot path, so it is declared to CI. The three files that drive `apply`'s gates against real databases were run anyway because the gates' reads moved: `comment-reactions.integration`, `apply-organization-ownership-gate.integration` and `apply.account-issuer-retirement.integration`, `Tests 16 passed`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 68 derived commands, plus the 11 declared WIDE-population families, 79 in all, each exit captured before any pipe.
  - 77 exited 0 on the first pass.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`: no `dist/` for packages this diff does not touch). After `pnpm build` both exited 0 on the same head.
  - `--ran`: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 68 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 68 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).`
- `node scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs --changed-from origin/main`: exit 0 (no anchored file in the change set).
- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`, the whole repository): exit 0, no findings.

## Acceptance notes

- **Deviation from the claim's file surface: two existing test files.** `apply.organization-ownership-refusal.test.ts` and `apply.account-issuer-json-refusal.test.ts` are outside the claimed surface. Their fixtures could not represent a real drift entry, and the change made that visible (see "What changed"). They needed a one-key fixture correction, plus one added assertion in the issuer control so it can no longer pass on an unrelated exit 1.
- **Reads added, measured as harmless.** A human-face `apply` (with or without `--allow-destructive`) and `plan` now make a gate's read whenever that gate's drop is listed. Before, a run without the flag made none. For the issuer gate that read is the pre-flight's walk of `sys_account`, which it already made on every `--allow-destructive` run. With the flag, the listing and the gate share one read, so the count is unchanged. That is pinned, and the existing issuer control's `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` still holds. `--json` makes no new read.
- **Unchanged by design (PR #24954's shape).** While a gate holds a drop, the other destructive entries keep the differ's `--allow-destructive` sentence on their own lines; each gate's footer line counts them as waiting for it. The category heading `Destructive (requires --allow-destructive)` is unchanged.
- **Held off, still printing.** The boot's `[schema-drift]` lines (#24956, the engine lane) still print `"os migrate apply --allow-destructive" to drop it.` during `apply`'s flush, in the same run as the new lines.
- **Out of scope, measured, for the PM to route.** On the `issuer` database, `apply --allow-destructive`'s pre-flight report prints `issuers [(none)]` for two rows whose stored issuers are `https://idp-a.example` and `https://idp-b.example`. `os migrate account-issuer` on the same database prints `issuers [https://idp-a.example, https://idp-b.example]`. The pre-flight `apply` uses (`probeAccountIdentityCollisions`, plugin-auth) reads through `engine.find`, which projects only the declared fields, and v18 no longer declares `issuer`. Not changed here: the refusal path is held off.
